title: Accuracy Before Speed
summary: Type common words for accuracy first, because speed grows out of clean, repeated movements.

explain.goal: Type everyday words at a pace where you make very few mistakes.
why: Speed comes from accuracy and rhythm. Every mistake makes you stop, back up, and retype, and that costs more time than typing a little slower would have.
Muscle memory forms when you repeat correct movements. Repeating a mistake trains the mistake, so it is better to slow down until the right movement is the easy one.
That is also why you should not look at the keyboard. Looking makes you type for your eyes. Your fingers learn faster when they have to find the keys themselves.
The lessons so far passed at 90 to 92 percent accuracy. This one asks for 95, because clean typing is the foundation for going faster.
how: Aim for accuracy first. If you are missing keys, slow down until you are hitting nearly all of them.
Once you are consistently accurate, raise your speed a little at a time.
Keep your eyes on the text, and let each finger return home after every reach.

mistakes.mistake: Speeding up before you are accurate
mistakes.reason: Each mistake costs a pause and a correction, which adds up to more time than a slower, clean pace.

mistakes.mistake: Looking at the keyboard to check
mistakes.reason: It slows your rhythm and stops your fingers from learning the keys by feel.

mistakes.mistake: Ignoring your mistakes and pushing on
mistakes.reason: If you keep repeating a wrong movement, that is the one that becomes a habit.

explain.recap: Accuracy first, then speed. Clean, repeated movements build the muscle memory that speed grows from.

title: Words That Swap Hands
summary: Type words that swap hands often, because alternating hands makes typing smoother and quicker.

explain.goal: Type words where your hands take turns on almost every letter.
why: When your hands alternate, one hand is already getting into position while the other is pressing. That overlap gives typing a smooth, flowing rhythm.
Real text is full of words like these, so practicing them trains the rhythm you will use every day.
Words are also where all your single-key practice comes together: each finger has to take its turn on time, and that is what a steady rhythm is.
how: Let your hands take turns. As one presses, the other is already getting ready.
Keep the rhythm even instead of bursting on easy letters and stalling on hard ones.
Look at the text, and keep your accuracy above the pass mark.

mistakes.mistake: Rushing the easy letters and stumbling on the hard ones
mistakes.reason: An uneven rhythm breaks your flow. Steady beats bursts.

mistakes.mistake: Tensing your hands to go faster
mistakes.reason: Tension slows the fingers. A loose, even rhythm is quicker in the long run.

explain.recap: Alternating hands makes typing smooth. Keep the rhythm even and let the hands take turns.
